History · 3 lessons

Make sense of years and calendars

Start with century numbers, understand leap-year rules, then follow the calendar reform that changed Britain’s dates.

By Biel Sardà · Published 30 Sept 2026 · Suggest a correction

What you will learn

A date looks precise, but understanding it takes a little context. First learn how years are grouped. Next explore the rule that keeps a calendar close to the seasons. Finally see why a historical date needs its calendar as well as its numbers.

Before you start: No previous history reading required. The century examples use positive CE years.

  • Place a positive CE year in its century.
  • Apply the Gregorian leap-year exception.
  • Distinguish a calendar date change from elapsed time.

Keep these ideas handy

Century
A period of one hundred years; conventional CE centuries begin in years ending in 01.
Leap year
A calendar year with an extra day, governed here by Gregorian rules.
Calendar reform
A change to the rules used to label and organise dates.
